Stryy New Jewish Cemetery

Jewish Cemetery · Lviv Oblast, Ukraine

Demolished. Flagging a likely data error up front: this record's address and coordinates point to Komarno, a separate town in Lviv Oblast, not to Stryy — the source data appears to have copied the wrong location for this cemetery; coordinates were left as given in the source rather than substituted, since this was not independently verified. Historically, Jewish presence in Stryy dates to 1563, and the community grew alongside the town's economy and Zionist movement to a peak of nearly 11,000 (about 30 percent of the town) by 1921. Occupation from July 1941 brought an early massacre, a ghetto in 1942 holding nearly 9,700 Jews, and its liquidation in mid-1943 with roughly 3,000 killed; this cemetery itself is presumed demolished during or after WWII, its site now overbuilt with a car service.
